title: fix: bill fractional image usage instead of truncating it to zero
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
## What

`parseUsageHeaders()` used `parseInt` for `promptImageTokens`/`completionImageTokens`. On Replicate image-editing routes (FLUX.2 Pro/Max) these carry megapixel counts, not integer token counts, and are almost never whole numbers — `parseInt("0.3072", 10)` is `0`.

## Impact

- Reference-image edit requests silently billed $0 for the input image's megapixel cost, on every call.
- FLUX.2 Pro: leaks only when its Replicate fallback serves (Azure is primary).
- FLUX.2 Max (pending in #14811): Replicate is primary, so this would leak on every edit request.

## Fix

Add `promptImageTokens`/`completionImageTokens` to the existing float-parsing allowlist (`FLOAT_USAGE_TYPES`), alongside the audio/video duration fields that already need it. Same fix shape, no behavior change for integer-valued usage (`parseFloat` and `parseInt` agree on whole numbers).

## Verification

- Added a regression test reproducing the exact truncation (`0.3072` → `0`, confirmed fixed)
- Full `gen.pollinations.ai` suite: 129 files, 2161 passed, 0 failed
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in `gen.pollinations.ai`
- Confirmed live against PR #14811 locally: reference-image requests billed the correct megapixel-based cost after this change instead of the same price as a zero-reference-image request
